reel.caption_cta: I'll show you how I made this -> Check my bio

style: 3D animated (Pixar-style CG) for 0-54.50 s (one 0.22 s black frame at 27.10 s); live-action handheld phone 'real me' tag 54.50-56.03 s (5 shots). Small white lowercase word-by-word captions, lower-middle; big cream clock timestamps during the night montage.
logline: Mom finds out her son blew $2,000 on clothes for a resale brand with 3 sales and gives him one week to earn it back; after all-nighters the orders explode, she ends up packing beside him, and he tells her 'We did it.'

hook.mechanic: Cold open on an angry parent bursting through the door with the son's wallet ('Nate! Where is all your money?'), a whip-pan between them and two whip-blur pans across the stock he bought - the stakes ($2,000), the conflict and the setting land in 4.5 s; hook title 'MOMMY SAID I'D FAIL' promises the reversal.
hook.first_line: Nate! Where is all your money?

blocks.description: Night grind: locked-off frontal desk shot with a big clock caption (11:48 PM -> 2:14 AM, digits glitching) - hoodies laid out, listings built on the laptop, mailers bagged; it turns into a stutter of 0.1 s jump cuts as the light flips between warm and moonlit blue. Wordless, music-driven.

Team montage: the same frontal two-shot of son and Mom packing side by side, match-cut through places and times of day (stockroom day/night, sunny yard with palms, brick wall), a kiss and a hug, 'More! Keep packing!' / 'I am!' over flash cuts as short as 0.08 s.

montage.description: Two montages: a solo night grind (time passing on one locked-off desk) and a 'same pose, different world' team montage after Mom switches sides.

stats.dead_air: None in the audio sense: music runs the full reel (silencedetect at -35 dB/0.4 s found no silence). Gaps with no dialogue (>= 1.5 s): 13.56-19.87 (6.3 s), 35.71-38.09 (2.4 s), 40.65-46.30 (5.6 s), 52.04-56.03 (4.0 s).

beats.summary: HOOK: Mom storms in with his wallet - 'Where is all your money?' 'I spent it!' 'On what?' 'My business!' - whip-pans across his stock.
Argument and challenge: $2,000 on clothes, phone shows 3 sales; 'Then prove it! One week... every dollar.' 'Fine.'
Night grind montage on one desk, clock running from 11:48 PM to 2:14 AM.
Low point: 'I spent everything.' Mom softens from the doorway - 'You don't have to prove anything to me.' 'Yes, I do.' Then: 'Wait...'
Breakthrough: crash zoom into his eye ('3'), notifications pour in, 'No way!', he runs to Mom: 'Orders!' 'How many?' 'Ten.'
Orders explode: stock multiplies 10-20-30; frantic packing together; Mom grabs the tee - 'You're too slow.' 'Wait! ...Okay!'
beats.emotion: chaos, comedy, Mom flips to ally

beats.summary: Team montage, match-cut across days and places; kiss, hug; 'More! Keep packing!' 'I am!'
Payoff: a room walled with boxes. 'We did it.' 'You did.' 'No. We did.' Closet stacked with parcels.
Real-me tag: real warehouse walk, the creator and (likely) his real mother doing the shocked pose, car, purple stock room; loops.

transcription: faster-whisper 'small' (CPU, int8), word timestamps; checked line by line against the burned-in word captions. Fixed 'Improve it' -> 'Then prove it', a second 'What?' -> 'Look!', dropped a 'So'; added 'Nate!' and the 45-48 s 'More! / Keep packing! / I am!' from captions only. Whisper's very short spans on 'Wait.' and 'Three!' (0.04-0.12 s) were widened to the caption timing, which lowers the words-per-second figure from 5.96 to the value below.
why_it_works: Instant stakes: a number ($2,000), a villain-ish parent with the wallet and a whip-pan across the stock - viewer knows who, what and why in 4.5 s.
Rapid-fire bickering (lines of 1-3 words, 0.2-0.5 s apart) played on mostly static two-shots; the speed of the cutting matches the speed of the talk.
Cartoon-big acting on the key beats only: Mom's ECU with bulging eyes, the chair flail, the screaming 'I am!' - between them the faces stay grounded.
The night montage sells effort without dialogue: one locked-off frame, a clock caption ticking, light flipping warm/blue, then stutter jump cuts as fatigue sets in.
A quiet low point ('You don't have to prove anything to me') gives the turn somewhere to come from, and the crash zoom into the eye makes '3 orders' feel huge.
The antagonist becomes the partner: Mom grabs the shirt ('You're too slow'), then the match-cut team montage shows them packing in the same pose across days and places.
Final line flips the opening blame into shared credit ('You did.' 'No. We did.'), an emotional button stronger than a revenge ending.
The real-life tag puts the creator and, likely, his real mother in the same 'shocked' pose, linking the cartoon to real life and to the 'Check my bio' CTA.
undetermined: Music not identified (music bed under the whole reel; only speech transcribed).

Night montage 16.40-19.80 s is one locked-off set-up with AI morph blends and jump cuts; jump cuts were counted where the light or the item on the desk changes all at once, so that count is approximate (+/- 3).
27.32-32.63 s judged one continuous take (frame differences stay smooth as he runs out to Mom).
33.88-39.85 s: the cut at 37.27 s sits inside sped-up packing in the same set-up; it could be a speed-ramp rather than a cut.
'More! / Keep packing! / I am!' (45-48 s) and 'Nate!' (0.4 s) are caption only, timings estimated; speakers inferred from faces.
'Yes!' at 8.34 s (son, off-screen) and 'Twenty. / Thirty.' (son, off-screen) speakers inferred.
The woman in the live-action tag is probably the creator's real mother; not confirmed.
